newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end lower on technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end lower on technicals.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board again Friday in a lackluster session, with the complex pressured by technical selling and pre-weekend profit taking after Thursday's reversal.
December slipped 6.6 cents to close at $2.662 per million British thermal units, barely above $2.66 support. January settled 5.4 cents lower at $2.644. Others also ended lower.

"We may not be done testing the lower end of the range, but it's too early to write off this market," said one Houston trader, noting technical sentiment grew more bearish this week but cold weather could quickly change opinions.
Most agreed the technical picture was damaged by December's reversal Thursday, when the spot contract edged to a new contract high but settled sharply lower.

But chartists had mixed opinions from here, particularly after the December close today just above near-support at $2.66. Some also noted that the longer-term trend was still up despite the sharp two-day slide.

Next support in December was pegged in the low-$2.50s. Resistance was seen at the $2.88 contract high and then at $2.92 and $2.98, prominent spot continuation chart highs set in late June and early July.

Cash sources said weekend Gulf Coast prices were down a couple of cents Friday to the mid-$2.70s. Midwest pipes slumped almost a dime to the mid-$2.60s on expectations for more seasonal weather early next week. New York city gate prices were quoted in the $3.10-25 area, down more than 10 cents from Thursday.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip slipped three cents to $2.186. NYMEX said 28,099 Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 30,620.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed one cent lower at $1.23, while deferreds finished down by 1.5 cents. NYMEX said 12 Alberta contracts traded compared with 112 on Thursday.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded but December ended down by seven cents at $2.54.

On the KCBT, December finished three cents lower at $2.56, while deferreds settled down by four to six cents. The December East/West spread narrowed by 3.6 cents to 10.2 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 379 contracts traded, up from Thursday's total of 273.
